card.hook: Picture a cruise ship parked so close you could wave at the people on deck, with blue water all around and Nevis sitting on the horizon behind it. That's Port Zante, a little waterfront quarter pushed out into Basseterre Bay.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 1.2 km east of Port Zante, and face west toward the port. For the classic close-up view, walk onto the promenade along the berthed piers and look out over the ships.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit a whole ship and the length of the pier into one frame. Switch to 1x for the entrance arch and the green-roofed plaza buildings. Try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out Nevis behind the ships.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, keep the horizon level, and put the ship's waterline along a lower grid line so the sea and sky feel balanced.
card.best_time: Try to shoot between ship arrivals. Two large ships can berth at once, and the promenade gets busy on those days. Give yourself a few minutes to stroll the length of the promenade too, because the angle on the ships changes as you go.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the pavement just outside the terminal exit with the 'St. Kitts' sign behind you, or in the plaza in front of the yellow arched building with the green roof and dome, with the 'Welcome to St. Kitts' lettering behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x and hold your phone a little high so the sign or arch fits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back on the plaza so the whole arch and the 'Welcome to St. Kitts' sign fit in the frame, while you stand in front of the arched building.
card.rules_and_safety: Some travellers report a man with a monkey charging for photos near the port (about $10 per person, according to one guide). That's a paid offer, so you can simply say no thanks.
card.challenge: Get one shot of a ship with a little water in front of it and Nevis behind it, then spin round and grab the green hills behind you.
card.good_to_know: Port Zante sits on about 15 acres of land reclaimed from the sea in 1995, which is why it feels like it's floating in the middle of the bay. Basseterre itself was founded by the French in 1627, so it's one of the older towns in the Eastern Caribbean. For a wider second shot, walk to the waterfront near the Treasury Building, where you can fit the cruise berths and the town into one view.

selfie_research.notes: The pages I found do not state any rule on selfie sticks or tripods at Port Zante, so none is reported. The 'ask someone' spot is inferred from traveller photo captions ('a feature in front of the archway') rather than from an explicit instruction, so exact standing position is approximate. Some reviews mention a man with a monkey charging for photos near the port (about $10 per person per one guide), which is a paid photo offer, not a selfie spot. Tripadvisor listing and blog descriptions are dated and may change.
